title: Normalized scalar-extension Hom degree maps
statement: Let $A,B$ be commutative rings, $\varphi:A\to B$ a ring homomorphism, and $\mathcal M_A,\mathcal M_B$ the module-sheaf categories on the one-object bottom-topology site [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $F:\mathcal M_A\to\mathcal M_B$ be additive, with equalities $h_M:F(M)=\operatorname{changeOfRings}_{\varphi}(M)$ and $F(a)=h_M\circ\operatorname{changeOfRingsHom}_{\varphi}(a)\circ h_N^{-1}$ for every morphism $a:M\to N$, where composition is written in diagrammatic order [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $F^\bullet$ be termwise extension, $H_A,H_B$ the shared Hom complexes with their chosen product projections into internal Homs [def-pur-hom-complex, def-pur-sheaf-hom], and let $\operatorname{pure}_M(b,x)$ and $\operatorname{ev}_p$ denote the transported pure tensor and identity-slice evaluation [def-pc-ring-hom-extension-shared-definitions]. For arbitrary cochain complexes $P,Q$ in $\mathcal M_A$ and every $n\in\mathbf Z$, there exists a morphism $t:F(H_A(P,Q)^n)\to H_B(F^\bullet P,F^\bullet Q)^n$ such that for every $p\in\mathbf Z$, site object $U$, $b,c\in B$, $f\in H_A(P,Q)^n(U)$ and $x\in P^p(U)$, $\operatorname{ev}_p(t(\operatorname{pure}_{H_A(P,Q)^n}(b,f)))(\operatorname{pure}_{P^p}(c,x))=\operatorname{pure}_{Q^{p+n}}(bc,\operatorname{ev}_p(f)(x))$. No differential compatibility is asserted.

proof.text: Construct the ordinary tensor-Hom linear map using Mathlib IsBaseChange.linearMapRightBaseChangeHom and LinearMap.liftBaseChangeEquiv. Identify the one-point internal Hom with linear maps by direct slice evaluation, and scalar extension with tensor product via the invertible bottom-topology sheafification unit. Conjugate the ordinary map by these linear equivalences and extend its value to the sole site object. Its normalization follows by cancellation of the equivalences on pure tensors. No invertibility characterization is needed or asserted.

Naturality of the sheafification unit and the specified morphism formula for F show that extended product projections preserve pure tensors. The target limiting fan supplied by homComplex_exists assembles the coordinate maps using Fan.IsLimit.lift; Fan.IsLimit.fac proves their normalization. No preservation of infinite products is assumed.

lean.statement: theorem ringHomExtension_degrees_exists {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B) (F : RingSiteModules A ⥤ RingSiteModules B) (h : ∀ M, F.obj M = SheafOfModules.changeOfRings (ringSiteMap φ) M) (hm : ∀ {M N} (f : M ⟶ N), F.map f = eqToHom (h M) ≫ SheafOfModules.changeOfRingsHom (ringSiteMap φ) M f ≫ eqToHom (h N).symm) (hF : F.Additive) (P Q : CochainComplex (RingSiteModules A) ℤ) (n : ℤ) : ∃ t : F.obj ((homComplex (R := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf A) P Q).X n) ⟶ (homComplex (R := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf B) ((ringExtensionComplex F hF).obj P) ((ringExtensionComplex F hF).obj Q)).X n, ∀ (p : ℤ) (U : (Discrete PUnit.{u + 1})ᵒᵖ) (b c : B) (f : (homComplex (R := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf A) P Q).X n |>.val.obj U) (x : (P.X p).val.obj U), ringHomEvaluate ((ringExtensionComplex F hF).obj P) ((ringExtensionComplex F hF).obj Q) n p U (t.val.app U (ringExtensionPure φ F h _ U b f)) (ringExtensionPure φ F h (P.X p) U c x) = ringExtensionPure φ F h (Q.X (p + n)) U (b * c) (ringHomEvaluate P Q n p U f x)
